title: Weekly Love Horoscopes For September 21 - 27 — Libra Season Starts
author: Leslie Hale
body:
Weekly Love Horoscopes For September 21 - 27 — Libra Season Starts
The weekly love horoscope for September 21 to 27, 2026 shows a great week for every zodiac sign's relationship, although the weekend looks a little dicey. Monday is a great day for getting together with someone special or socializing because the Sun sextiles Jupiter on September 21, a light and upbeat type of energy, which is a great way to start the week.
The Sun enters Libra on September 22. During Libra season, people are usually more focused on love and social activities than usual. When Mars begins its transit through Leo on September 27, prepare to feel more confident in yourself and eager to get out and about. The weekend has potential for things to go south because you may question your feelings for someone as the Sun opposes Neptune on Friday and becomes part of the Full Moon energy on the 26th. It'll be easy to default to thinking about the worst-case scenario, but try looking at things from a different perspective to avoid crashing out. The energy will soon pass.
Weekly love horoscopes for September 21 to 27, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
This week represents a turning point in your love life. The Sun’s opposition to Neptune will likely make you question a close relationship on Friday.
It is time to look at how your relationship is working, Aries. Or if you're single and looking, think about what your next step is. Choose the path of creativity and compassion over suspicion and mistrust if you can.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Venus is transiting through your 7th house of partners and is in its shadow period energy before it turns retrograde in October. That means you can expect to be deep in contemplation about your relationship this week.
The Full Moon and the Sun’s opposition to Neptune hits your 12th house of the subconscious this weekend. This will help you decide if you are with the right person, Taurus. It could also bring up issues and anger relating to past relationships. Do your best not to project.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
On September 22, the Sun’s entrance into Libra lights up your 5th house of love and romance. This is just the start of an entire astrological month of good times, Gemini.
On Saturday, the Aries Full Moon lights up the part of your chart dealing with friends and your social life. This is a weekend you'll want to spend with those who align with you mentally and emotionally.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Venus is transiting your 5th house of love, which is significant for your relationships. Including your relationship with yourself, Cancer!
Since Venus is getting closer to its retrograde phase, expect to start thinking about how you can bring some more romance into your relationship, especially if you've been with someone for a while.
I wouldn't be surprised if the Aries Full Moon triggers a conflict between your business and personal life at the end of the week. You may feel pulled in different directions. Hidden issues or resentments can erupt, so it’s important to maintain a clear head and not get lost in Neptune’s fog.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
It's a relatively quiet week for your love life, Leo. But no news is usually good news when it comes to astrology.
This weekend, the Sun’s opposition to Neptune lights up your 3rd house of communication and your 9th house of philosophy, learning, and travel. This is also where the Full Moon falls on Saturday, which tells me there is potential for travel or meeting someone who lives at a distance.
One thing I do see happening for you this week is a change of perspective.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
The Sun’s opposition to Neptune this week offers a glimpse into your personal self-esteem. The way you feel about yourself often dictates who you allow into your life, Virgo.
Saturday's Full Moon in Aries falls in your 8th house, which rules things like intimacy and money. This energy represents a transformation, so you may find yourself at a turning point in love this weekend.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Your birthday season has officially begun! The Sun-Neptune opposition this week will shed light on a current love interest or someone you would like to know better and how they are impacting your life.
On Saturday, the Full Moon lights up your partnership sector. While it may not be all fireworks right now, some reflection and simple appreciation of the small things lead to very positive results for you this week, Libra.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Your magnetism and intensity are at an all-time high with Venus transiting through your 1st house. If you don't feel attractive and emboldened this week, I'd be very surprised.
Scorpio, keep that same energy this weekend because if you have been idolizing someone, prepare for the Full Moon to bring you back down to earth. This doesn’t mean an ending is inevitable, but it does mean you may have to adjust your expectations a bit.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You may crave a far-away adventure and even make plans for one this week. But hey, what else is new?
The Full Moon lands in your 5th house of love this weekend. If things in a relationship seem different or not as fiery as you are used to, use this moon to reflect on whether or not you are truly aligned with your love interest or person of interest.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
This is the last week of Mars transiting your 7th house of partners. Once the planet of passion enters Leo, your 8th house, next week, things might not feel as exciting, so enjoy it while you can!
On Saturday, the Full Moon falls in your 4th house, which rules your foundation in life. This is a good weekend to really soak in the beauty in those around you. Don’t get drawn into negative emotions or game-playing, Capricorn.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
This is actually a great week for your love life, Aquarius. You're about to reach a turning point for the better as past tensions make way for a more balanced outlook.
The Aries Full Moon falls in your 3rd house on Saturday, making you feel more social and talkative this weekend. I think you're ready for a short adventure.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
The Sun leaves your 7th house of partners on Tuesday and enters your 8th house, which is far deeper and more profound energy.
Venus is transiting through Scorpio, which is a complementary sign for you. You may be interested in someone who lives at a distance or even in another country.
Over the weekend, the Aries moon sheds light on the condition of your personal self-worth and how this affects your romantic choices for better or worse.
Leslie Hale is a professional astrologer with over 30 years of experience specializing in astrological guidance to empower you with knowledge of future events, relationships, finances, and major life situations.

title: I'm having a quasi affair // micro cheating on husband
author: Anonymous
body:
“Micro cheating” is a bit slippery to define. In my parents’ day, in the 1980s, I imagine it would be removing your wedding ring when you attended a drinks party. Or failing to mention that you have a husband when someone offers to buy you a baby-cham at the bar. Nowadays there are many ways to micro-cheat with WhatsApp and social media, making it easier than ever.
A term popularised by the dating coach Melanie Schilling in 2017, micro cheating isn’t a one size fits all. What does and doesn’t count feels individual and varies between couples (is liking someone else’ s Instagram photos micro cheating?) I’d personally define it as the things you do or say which you know would upset your partner if they knew. A survey found 40 per cent of Brits believe that “developing any romantic feelings [even] without acting on them” is cheating. So perhaps calling it “micro” is just an attempt to make it sound less terrible than it really is.
The problem is: I think if most married couples were honest, they’d admit that they’ve thought that way about other people, and fantasised about sleeping with them. I’m not proud of it but I have been micro-cheating on my husband for 18 months.
Shorts
I’m 48 and have been married to Simon* for 22 years. We have two teenage boys. Simon is wedded to his work and we get on well, but I feel like we’re ships in the night. We spend too long on our laptops. We talk about how we need to prioritise one another but we’re too busy. We have stressful jobs, and at the end of the day, we tend to stare at our phones. Perimenopause hasn’t helped much either. I don’t fancy Simon and feel angry a lot.
A year and a half ago, I met Dean at a health and wellness conference in Corfu. I work in corporate hospitality and we were staying at a beautiful luxury hotel. Each day we’d attend talks about the ‘future of hospitality’, which was boring, but at 5pm everyone would meet for drinks.
On the second night of the conference, Dean and I ended up sitting together at the local taverna. He was Irish, in his late 40s, recently divorced and worked in PR. He lived in Bali, not the UK. I remember noticing him right away; he was good-looking, but I also dismissed him as annoying. He kept name-dropping famous people that he’d worked with.
Then after a while, perhaps influenced by three glasses of wine, we got chatting. We had a lot in common. We loved 90s dance music. We’d gone clubbing to the same places in our youth. We loved the same films – any Steve Martin comedy. I realised that talking about this stuff was something I missed. Simon and I were in functional parent mode; we talked about what to eat for tea and whether the boys were going to fail their exams.
Dean and I got drunk and we swapped numbers. I felt 18, like I was in this fantasy where I was desirable again. To be honest, I didn’t think I fancied people anymore until I met Dean.
When I woke up the following day, I felt guilty. Why had I found it so easy to give Dean my number? I told myself he would be a “useful work contact”, and vowed to give him a wide berth. On the second night, however, when I was sitting at the bar, quite drunk yet again (I was letting my hair down; I might even have been smoking too…), I got a text from Dean. “I was hoping we could meet up. Fancy coming to my room for a nightcap?”
To be honest, I was stunned. I’d not seen him all day and thought he’d been flirting with me the night before because a lot of people in our industry can be super friendly. I told him that I’d give it a miss. Then he sent another text saying he was disappointed – “I thought we had chemistry,” he said.
At that point I should have fully shut it down but instead I typed: “I really like you. I would love to come to your room but I can’t do it as I know what will happen. I’m sorry.” The reality was that because I was away on my own, in a different country, I felt like I should have a holiday fling!
I fell asleep and the next day got a text from Dean saying that he was leaving early as he had to go home for a work meeting. I felt flat, like I’d missed an opportunity. If I’d slept with Dean, then probably the whole thing would have finished right there. But instead, that’s when we started messaging one another in earnest.
We used Instagram messenger, not WhatsApp – where I text most people. I’ve never actually texted a man who wasn’t Simon, not romantically at least and to begin with I was disoriented. Sometimes Dean would text about work-related things. So he’d be sharing a client and then he would be telling me that he was feeling sad because he’d injured his knee.
He would send me selfies and photos of everything in his life. Not naked ones, but just a diary showing what he was doing. We messaged a lot. It was a running conversation that we picked up as soon as we were both online. I started putting kisses at the end of each message. I also confided in him about feeling lonely.
It felt like cheating because I don’t usually put kisses at the end of messages. Also, I was finding that Dean was cropping up more often in my mind, and I’d wonder what he was up to. But he was also so far away that it felt safe. We didn’t have to take anything further, and Simon didn’t have to find out.
At other times I convinced myself it wasn’t cheating as Dean would share information about a woman he was seeing. Weirdly, I felt hurt but knew I couldn’t – I’m married!
The life that Dean was living seemed idyllic and a long way away from me putting washing in the machine and avoiding Simon, who was often in a permanent sulk. I should have felt guiltier, but as the weeks passed, I justified it because I was feeling low. Our marriage had deteriorated. I was comparing Simon to Dean and Dean was just a fantasy. But it felt strangely intimate too. He’d share songs that we both loved. I found myself getting obsessive. I knew it was ridiculous. Months passed and each morning I’d wait for a message, feeling disappointed if there was nothing there.
Simon was now working every hour of the day; I mean, I assumed he was. I would regularly delete the chats with Dean but Simon has never been one to check my phone. One time my son Aidan picked it up and I hadn’t deleted the conversation. He said: “Who is this dude?” I blushed. “He’s just a work friend. We message about work stuff,” I’d said. Luckily, he didn’t mention it again.
When I spoke to female friends, they were aghast. Why was I bothering to text this guy who lived so far away? What was his agenda? Money? Did he have any intention of meeting up with me? What was I getting out of the whole thing? It was hard to explain. I was getting friendship, and a bit of flirtation thrown in for good measure.
With micro-cheating, you get “micro-doses” of guilt. I justified it because I was bored. Because Simon and I didn’t have sex. Because I felt old and like time was running out. The truth was that I felt closer to Dean than to Simon after 12 months of texting. We knew each other really well.
He would often say things like “if we’d met back in the 90s, we would have been an item.” But he never made plans to come to the UK, even though I knew that he could. There were times when I tried to push things, suggesting that perhaps I should come to Bali. I increasingly felt like my feelings were much stronger than his.
Then one morning a couple of months ago, when I was getting ready to drive to the garden centre, I checked my phone and Dean had sent me a photo of his penis! I felt like perhaps he’d sent it by mistake. Luckily, it disappeared as Instagram has a one-view feature. “I’m sorry,” Dean texted later. I felt so mixed about it. I did fancy him. I sometimes thought about what it would be like. I dreamt about it, in fact.
The photo did feel like a line had been crossed. I also felt like he was maybe playing me; if I didn’t message for a few days, he’d double down and send me a long voice note. I’d hear his voice, immediately felt closer and more obsessive again.
But the photo made me decide to go cold turkey. I blocked him – of course there was no resolution because we didn’t have a relationship in the first place but I felt like I was going mad. Then, after two weeks, I unblocked him and messaged. “I can’t stop thinking about you. How’s work?” I knew it was stupid. That was last month.
I know I have to put energy into my marriage but I feel so over it. The energy I get from Dean makes me feel alive. Today I am still “micro cheating”. Except it doesn’t feel quite so micro anymore. It feels like a massive lie because it’s been going on so long. I keep telling myself it’s pointless. That I am betraying Simon. That I owe it to my sons to give it up and make more of an effort at home. There are days when I feel Dean and I will meet up in real life and others when I think he’s stringing a whole host of women along.
He’s an enigma in many ways. The opposite of the man I’ve shared a bed with for so many years. I know that I’m wasting time. But I’m also totally addicted. I sometimes daydream a scenario where we meet. I also know that if we did meet, there’d be too much pressure on the whole thing, as my expectations of him are way too high. I have sort of made him into an ideal partner, filled in the blanks and ensured he has all the things I look for. He’d never be able to live up to that high standard anyway.

We loved the same films – any Steve Martin comedy. I realised that talking about this stuff was something I missed. Simon and I were in functional parent mode; we talked about what to eat for tea and whether the boys were going to fail their exams.
Dean and I got drunk and we swapped numbers. I felt 18, like I was in this fantasy where I was desirable again. To be honest, I didn’t think I fancied people anymore until I met Dean.
When I woke up the following day, I felt guilty. Why had I found it so easy to give Dean my number? I told myself he would be a “useful work contact”, and vowed to give him a wide berth. On the second night, however, when I was sitting at the bar, quite drunk yet again (I was letting my hair down; I might even have been smoking too…), I got a text from Dean. “I was hoping we could meet up. Fancy coming to my room for a nightcap?”
To be honest, I was stunned. I’d not seen him all day and thought he’d been flirting with me the night before because a lot of people in our industry can be super friendly. I told him that I’d give it a miss. Then he sent another text saying he was disappointed – “I thought we had chemistry,” he said.
At that point I should have fully shut it down but instead I typed: “I really like you. I would love to come to your room but I can’t do it as I know what will happen. I’m sorry.” The reality was that because I was away on my own, in a different country, I felt like I should have a holiday fling!
I fell asleep and the next day got a text from Dean saying that he was leaving early as he had to go home for a work meeting. I felt flat, like I’d missed an opportunity. If I’d slept with Dean, then probably the whole thing would have finished right there. But instead, that’s when we started messaging one another in earnest.
We used Instagram messenger, not WhatsApp – where I text most people. I’ve never actually texted a man who wasn’t Simon, not romantically at least and to begin with I was disoriented. At other times I convinced myself it wasn’t cheating as Dean would share information about a woman he was seeing. Weirdly, I felt hurt but knew I couldn’t – I’m married!
The life that Dean was living seemed idyllic and a long way away from me putting washing in the machine and avoiding Simon, who was often in a permanent sulk. I should have felt guiltier, but as the weeks passed, I justified it because I was feeling low. Our marriage had deteriorated. I was comparing Simon to Dean and Dean was just a fantasy. But it felt strangely intimate too. He’d share songs that we both loved. I found myself getting obsessive. I knew it was ridiculous. Months passed and each morning I’d wait for a message, feeling disappointed if there was nothing there.
Simon was now working every hour of the day; I mean, I assumed he was. I would regularly delete the chats with Dean but Simon has never been one to check my phone. One time my son Aidan picked it up and I hadn’t deleted the conversation. He said: “Who is this dude?” I blushed. “He’s just a work friend. We message about work stuff,” I’d said. Luckily, he didn’t mention it again.
When I spoke to female friends, they were aghast. Why was I bothering to text this guy who lived so far away? What was his agenda? Money? Did he have any intention of meeting up with me? What was I getting out of the whole thing? It was hard to explain. I was getting friendship, and a bit of flirtation thrown in for good measure.

I sometimes thought about what it would be like. I dreamt about it, in fact.
The photo did feel like a line had been crossed. I also felt like he was maybe playing me; if I didn’t message for a few days, he’d double down and send me a long voice note. I’d hear his voice, immediately felt closer and more obsessive again.

That I owe it to my sons to give it up and make more of an effort at home. There are days when I feel Dean and I will meet up in real life and others when I think he’s stringing a whole host of women along.
He’s an enigma in many ways. The opposite of the man I’ve shared a bed with for so many years. I know that I’m wasting time. But I’m also totally addicted. I sometimes daydream a scenario where we meet. I also know that if we did meet, there’d be too much pressure on the whole thing, as my expectations of him are way too high. I have sort of made him into an ideal partner, filled in the blanks and ensured he has all the things I look for. He’d never be able to live up to that high standard anyway.

title: Dear Abby | Good neighbor learns inclusivity has limits
author: Dear Abby
body:
Dear Abby | Good neighbor learns inclusivity has limits
Today's advice from Dear Abby.
DEAR ABBY: I am a single woman in a friendly neighborhood. Every month, I have the neighbors over for dinner and a movie. I like to be inclusive — bring the kids, bring the dogs! One couple recently had their elderly mom move in, and I installed a ramp so she could join us. Babies cry, dogs bark, women breastfeed, but all are welcome. I put sleeping bags on the floor for the kids to sit on while grownups sit on the couches. Cleanup is a bear, but every squished meatball on the floor reminds me how much I love everyone.
Recently, a new couple moved in, so of course I invited them and their 6-year-old to join us. They warned me that he has severe autism, but I told them everyone is welcome, that he wouldn’t be expected to be quiet and that the house is thoroughly kid-proofed. When the family showed up to join us, their child was horrible, even by my nonexistent standards for kiddo behavior. He screamed, threw food, bit, spit and hit the other kids and the dogs for an hour. Finally, everyone started to leave before the movie was over. The boy’s parents really did try their best, and I was genuinely sympathetic. They apologized the next day and said that if they were welcome in the future, they would alternate one parent staying home with their son while the other joined us. That sounds reasonable, but I don’t like it. I can’t be inclusive just when it suits me. They have since invited me to their home for dinner, and their son was just as bad there, banishing my thoughts that maybe it was just a strange house he was reacting to. I don’t know what to do with all this. I’m looking for a magic wand. Any suggestions?
— NEIGHBORLY IN THE EAST
DEAR NEIGHBORLY: You are a caring, lovely person, but there is no magic wand that will make that child’s severe autism and behavior problems go away. Because you are determined to entertain the entire family, the practical solution would be to invite them and their son over on another evening when other children and pets won’t be at risk of injury. Your movie night will be history if it is disrupted like that again. While I commend you for wanting to befriend the family, I think the parents had the right solution.
** ** **
DEAR ABBY: I’m 70 now, and many of my friends and family spend our time together complaining about their various ailments. I, too, have had some problems but do not make them a part of our visits unless I’m asked about them. How can I rethink how to make these times more positive for everyone involved?
— POSITIVE IN OREGON
DEAR POSITIVE: Sometimes, people of a certain age talk about their health problems because they have become less active and can find little else to talk about. To keep the energy flowing in a more positive direction, help your friends find hobbies and other interests to discuss. Even if they have medical issues, most people can manage quiet activities like board games, card games, a book club or a knitting circle. If all else fails, you can always ask them about their families as a change of subject.

title: Love Horoscope Today, September 20, 2026: What the stars say about your love life
author: TOI Astrology; Sep
body:
Each sign of the zodiac has its own set of traits that help to define their personalities and set them apart from each other. Wouldn't it be nice to know what the universe has planned for you at the beginning of the day? Keep reading to find out if today will be lucky for you.
ARIES
Don’t hide your heart to avoid an uncomfortable conflict. If anything is bothering you, say so instead of pretending it’s okay. But silence in matters of the heart is more expensive than truth. If you are with someone, your feelings matter too. If you're unattached don't be with someone who will simply provide you brief serenity. The things you actually desire today, writing them down might help you listen.
TAURUS
You’re not hard to love—you just need someone who can see you straight. Today, let go of blaming yourself for the space between you and another. People in partnerships need to inquire if they feel accepted as who they really are. Alone? If love is not the union of two but of opposing forces, do not let the adjustment of your wants be the price of someone’s comfort. To be chosen, one cannot help but recoil.
GEMINI
Emotional boldness is the beginning of romantic clarity. If you are perplexed today, the answer might not be in guesses but in questions or statements of the genuine thing. 
If you’re in a partnership, identify what’s bugging you, instead of letting it fester in your thoughts too long. By myself? Ask straight, don’t read signs that may have never meant a thing. When you are your real self, love flows more readily. Find your voice.”
CANCER
Give yourself permission to crave what is emotionally authentic. If you are tired of it, do not force yourself strong. Stop stating “that’s all right” in a partnership when it is not. Single? If distance isn't a good fit for you, don't lie and say it is. Be upfront about what you want. Today feelings that have been put down will come up. Don't be frightened to want something real. That doesn't make you needy. It makes you human. Don’t downplay it, to hide your truth.
LEO
Love is not passions that fluctuate with the weather. If you have a relationship, take note if the push-pull dynamic is draining you. If you are single, stop pursuing confused signals. Real concern is constant and not ambiguous. Don’t look for meaning in today’s upheaval; enjoy serenity instead. Love isn’t about trying to figure out where you stand, and if it makes you feel worried rather than settled, then that’s not something you want to attach yourself to.
VIRGO
Attraction can’t exist without emotional safety. Question yourself today: do you only feel good in your connection when things are happy, or even when things are quiet? If you are in a relationship, pay attention to whether you are being noticed or simply being complimented. If you’re single, don’t pursue charm without the consistency check. Looks may pull you in, but safety is what makes you remain. Choose someone who makes you feel peaceful.
LIBRA
You don’t need to waste energy that is not going to return to you. “Be careful where you put your efforts today. In a relationship: Are you always the one making contact with someone? If you are single, forget about chasing a person who always takes ages to reply or just replies with short messages. You are not needy. You are just over-giving in places that are not receiving. Love is supposed to be a two-way street. If it simply doesn’t seem mutual, it’s not your responsibility to convince someone that you’re worthy of love.
SCORPIO
Remain in touch with your emotional reality. Your true feelings count today, even if they are inconvenient. In a relationship, don’t conceal your sensations of discomfort just to maintain the facade of peace. When you’re single, communicate what you really want — even if that sounds painfully vulnerable. No need to express how you feel about them to be valid. Be honest with yourself first, and people will be more likely to relate to you.
SAGITTARIUS
Today is about owning those feelings! Don't apologize for how you feel. If you are with somebody, tell before it gets to you. And if you’re single, be honest about what you want, instead of playing games, or waiting for things to happen. Hid Away: you will not save yourself; you will only keep delaying your true horizon. Even if it seems a little raw or uncomfortable, speak out for yourself today. The proper individuals will hear what you say and will not hold it against you.
CAPRICORN
Being with someone can be valuable if you trust what your body feels, not what they say. It is a simple thing to say which feels smooth sometimes, nevertheless your gut instinct tends to know the truth time and time again. If you are in a relationship, you will learn to listen to how your body feels throughout the chats; if you are single, in contrast, you will pay attention to how you feel after meeting someone: relaxed or nervous? This is not the day for flowery speeches or expensive promises.
AQUARIUS
A moment of feeling can open the tiniest of cracks, and that can open everything. Today, therefore, speak what you think rather than what sounds polite. If you are in a relationship, stop the act; if you are single, stop the witty replies and say something that could actually matter. That one honest sentence can change everything – even if it feels small it can truly enhance that bond. don’t wait for the perfect time. Say what’s on your heart right now while it is still real.
PISCES
Do not plead for love. Let love be something you build. Today, it’s time to ask why if you’re the only one working hard. If you are in a relationship, make sure both of you are working on it. If you’re single and you’re overthinking your worthiness in terms of who comes back and who doesn’t, meaningful connections are only made through mutual caring, not hope. You don't need to work more merely to be wanted. All you have to do is to insist on being wanted.

Don’t hide your heart to avoid an uncomfortable conflict. If anything is bothering you, say so instead of pretending it’s okay. But silence in matters of the heart is more expensive than truth. If you are with someone, your feelings matter too. If you're unattached don't be with someone who will simply provide you brief serenity. The things you actually desire today, writing them down might help you listen.
TAURUS
You’re not hard to love—you just need someone who can see you straight. Today, let go of blaming yourself for the space between you and another. People in partnerships need to inquire if they feel accepted as who they really are. Alone? If love is not the union of two but of opposing forces, do not let the adjustment of your wants be the price of someone’s comfort. To be chosen, one cannot help but recoil.
GEMINI
Emotional boldness is the beginning of romantic clarity. If you are perplexed today, the answer might not be in guesses but in questions or statements of the genuine thing. 
If you’re in a partnership, identify what’s bugging you, instead of letting it fester in your thoughts too long. By myself? Ask straight, don’t read signs that may have never meant a thing. When you are your real self, love flows more readily. Find your voice.”
CANCER
Give yourself permission to crave what is emotionally authentic. If you are tired of it, do not force yourself strong. Stop stating “that’s all right” in a partnership when it is not. Single? If distance isn't a good fit for you, don't lie and say it is. Be upfront about what you want. Today feelings that have been put down will come up. Don't be frightened to want something real. That doesn't make you needy. It makes you human. Don’t downplay it, to hide your truth.
LEO
Love is not passions that fluctuate with the weather. If you have a relationship, take note if the push-pull dynamic is draining you. If you are single, stop pursuing confused signals. Real concern is constant and not ambiguous. Don’t look for meaning in today’s upheaval; enjoy serenity instead. Love isn’t about trying to figure out where you stand, and if it makes you feel worried rather than settled, then that’s not something you want to attach yourself to.
VIRGO
Attraction can’t exist without emotional safety. Question yourself today: do you only feel good in your connection when things are happy, or even when things are quiet? If you are in a relationship, pay attention to whether you are being noticed or simply being complimented. If you’re single, don’t pursue charm without the consistency check. Looks may pull you in, but safety is what makes you remain. Choose someone who makes you feel peaceful.
LIBRA
You don’t need to waste energy that is not going to return to you. “Be careful where you put your efforts today. In a relationship: Are you always the one making contact with someone? If you are single, forget about chasing a person who always takes ages to reply or just replies with short messages. You are not needy. You are just over-giving in places that are not receiving. Love is supposed to be a two-way street. If it simply doesn’t seem mutual, it’s not your responsibility to convince someone that you’re worthy of love.
SCORPIO
Remain in touch with your emotional reality. Your true feelings count today, even if they are inconvenient. In a relationship, don’t conceal your sensations of discomfort just to maintain the facade of peace. When you’re single, communicate what you really want — even if that sounds painfully vulnerable. No need to express how you feel about them to be valid. Be honest with yourself first, and people will be more likely to relate to you.
SAGITTARIUS
Today is about owning those feelings! Don't apologize for how you feel. If you are with somebody, tell before it gets to you. And if you’re single, be honest about what you want, instead of playing games, or waiting for things to happen. Hid Away: you will not save yourself; you will only keep delaying your true horizon. Even if it seems a little raw or uncomfortable, speak out for yourself today. The proper individuals will hear what you say and will not hold it against you.
CAPRICORN
Being with someone can be valuable if you trust what your body feels, not what they say. It is a simple thing to say which feels smooth sometimes, nevertheless your gut instinct tends to know the truth time and time again. If you are in a relationship, you will learn to listen to how your body feels throughout the chats; if you are single, in contrast, you will pay attention to how you feel after meeting someone: relaxed or nervous? This is not the day for flowery speeches or expensive promises.
AQUARIUS
A moment of feeling can open the tiniest of cracks, and that can open everything. Today, therefore, speak what you think rather than what sounds polite. If you are in a relationship, stop the act; if you are single, stop the witty replies and say something that could actually matter. That one honest sentence can change everything – even if it feels small it can truly enhance that bond. don’t wait for the perfect time. Say what’s on your heart right now while it is still real.
PISCES
Do not plead for love. Let love be something you build. Today, it’s time to ask why if you’re the only one working hard. If you are in a relationship, make sure both of you are working on it. If you’re single and you’re overthinking your worthiness in terms of who comes back and who doesn’t, meaningful connections are only made through mutual caring, not hope. You don't need to work more merely to be wanted. All you have to do is to insist on being wanted.

title: Weekly Love Horoscope, September 21 to September 27, 2026: Romantic clarity may shape your emotional journey this week
author: Kishori Sud
body:
Love feels more social and joyful this week. Singles may meet someone through friends, gatherings, or shared interests, while couples can reconnect by making time for laughter and enjoyable experiences together. Let romance feel lighter rather than turning every moment into a serious discussion.
Weekly Love Horoscope, September 21 to September 27, 2026: Romantic clarity may shape your emotional journey this week
Weekly Love Horoscope, September 21 to September 27, 2026. Find what these predictions have in store for you.
Love Tip: Make space for fun and genuine companionship.
Crystal Remedy: Carnelian: Carry it during social outings to encourage confidence, warmth, and openness.
Emotional maturity becomes important in relationships. You may need to respond calmly to a sensitive situation rather than reacting immediately. Singles could be attracted to someone emotionally grounded and dependable.
Love Tip: Express your feelings without allowing them to control your response.
Crystal Remedy: Amazonite: Keep it close during important conversations to encourage balanced communication.
Romantic uncertainty may leave you questioning someone's intentions. Avoid filling gaps in communication with assumptions. Singles should take time to understand a new connection, while couples may benefit from discussing concerns directly.
Love Tip: Look for clarity instead of creating your own answers.
Crystal Remedy: Fluorite: Place it near your bedside to encourage clear thinking and emotional discernment.
A strong sense of mutual affection can develop this week. Singles may encounter someone who seems genuinely receptive, while couples can strengthen their bond through honest conversations and shared plans.
Love Tip: Meet each other halfway instead of expecting one person to carry the relationship.
Crystal Remedy: Rhodonite: Carry it as a reminder of compassion, reciprocity, and emotional balance.
A fresh romantic chapter may be calling you. Singles could feel drawn toward an unexpected connection, while couples may benefit from trying something new together. Don't let fear of uncertainty prevent you from experiencing something different.
Love Tip: Take a romantic chance without abandoning your boundaries.
Crystal Remedy: Sunstone: Keep it with you on dates or social occasions to encourage confidence and positive energy.
A sweet message, unexpected attraction, or emotionally refreshing moment could brighten your week. Singles may discover interest through a gentle interaction, while couples can benefit from expressing affection more openly.
Love Tip: Pay attention to small gestures; they can reveal genuine interest.
Crystal Remedy: Pink Opal: Keep it near your personal space to encourage tenderness and emotional openness.
You may seek greater stability and clarity in love. Established relationships could focus on commitment, shared values, or future plans. Singles may be drawn toward someone whose intentions feel serious rather than uncertain.
Love Tip: Choose relationships that respect your values and boundaries.
Crystal Remedy: Howlite: Keep it beside your bed to encourage calm communication and thoughtful choices.
You may want greater control or certainty within your romantic life. Healthy boundaries are useful, but avoid becoming overly controlling when emotions feel uncertain. Singles can benefit from being confident about what they want without trying to force an outcome.
Love Tip: Lead with confidence, not control.
Crystal Remedy: Tiger Eye: Carry it when you need confidence while maintaining emotional balance.
You may feel emotionally tired but still hopeful about love. If you've been through repeated disappointments, this week asks you to protect your heart without completely closing it. Couples may need patience while working through a lingering issue.
Love Tip: Protect your energy while leaving room for genuine connection.
Crystal Remedy: Red Jasper: Keep it close when you need grounding, resilience, and emotional steadiness.
Romantic boundaries may need strengthening. Someone could challenge your position or make you question what you truly want. Singles should avoid chasing validation, while couples can strengthen trust by standing up for their needs respectfully.
Love Tip: Don't compromise your core needs just to maintain harmony.
Crystal Remedy: Black Tourmaline: Keep it near your personal space as a reminder to maintain healthy emotional boundaries.
The past may return through a message, meeting, or unexpected reminder. A familiar connection could bring warmth, but ask yourself whether it belongs in your present or simply carries sentimental value.
Love Tip: Let nostalgia inform you without allowing it to make the decision for you.
Crystal Remedy: Aquamarine: Carry it when revisiting old connections to encourage emotional clarity and calm.
Love takes on a more serious and secure tone. Couples may discuss family, long-term plans, or building a stronger future together. Singles may be attracted to someone who offers stability and genuine commitment.
Love Tip: Look for consistency that can support a lasting relationship.
Crystal Remedy: Green Jade: Keep it in your bedroom or carry it to symbolize harmony, stability, and enduring affection.
Kishori Sud
(Certified Tarot Card Reader & Crystal Healer, Founder at EnigmaTarotTribe ™)
- Kishori Sud is a spiritual practitioner, intuitive guide, and journalist with over five years of experience in tarot reading and holistic healing. A senior visualiser with an advertising agency turned journalist turned tarot reader, she brings a unique blend of creativity, storytelling, and intuition to her work. She has worked with leading media organisations including IANS, Jagran, and The Times of India. She is IPHM-certified in Tarot Reading and Crystal Healing, and also holds certifications in Spell Casting, Face Reading, and Palmistry, making her a well-rounded expert in the spiritual space. Having guided more than 10,000 clients, Kishori is known for her accurate insights and practical approach to spirituality. Her readings focus on clarity, emotional balance, and actionable guidance rather than just predictions. She specialises in karmic debt clearance, life path guidance, and personalised remedies tailored to individual energy and real-life situations. Kishori is the founder of Enigma Tarot Tribe, where she offers highly customised tarot consultations, crystal combinations, and spiritual remedies designed specifically for each individual’s concerns—be it love, career, healing, or manifestation. Her approach to customisation ensures that every solution aligns deeply with the client’s unique energy and life path. You can connect with her on Instagram at @enigmatarottribe and explore her customised services and crystal offerings at www.enigmatarottribe.comRead More

title: Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Sunday, September 20: That Conversation Won't Wait Much Longer
author: Kate Rose
body:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Sunday, September 20: That Conversation Won't Wait Much Longer
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for September 20, 2026. The Capricorn Moon squares Mercury in Libra on Sunday, encouraging you to ask for what you need in your love life.
This energy is all about emotional reassurance. To feel confident in your relationship, you need to know your feelings are reciprocated. Rather than guessing how the other person feels, ask. If you want to know if they love you, this is the day to find out. If you’re hoping to talk about the future, it’s time to bring up that conversation. No matter where you stand in your relationship, it’s better to know for sure.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Sunday, September 20, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be clear on your reasons, Aries. While you're searching for genuine love, you must be mindful of your reasons. This means that despite your desire for love or connection, you may also be looking for validation in your relationship.
Honor this very human need to know that you and your partner both value this connection. On Sunday, ask them how they feel. This will help you have the clarity you need and feel more secure in the future.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Honor your need for emotional safety, Taurus. Love is always a risk; however, that doesn’t mean you should take a chance without the knowledge to back it up.
Before you take a leap of faith, make sure the person you’re leaping with is going to do the same. On Sunday, don’t be afraid to talk about what you imagine your life will look like together, or the kinds of changes you’re both craving. This will help you feel confident that the only risk you’re taking is a new beginning together.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Don’t be afraid to talk it out, Gemini. Talking is one of your strengths, but you must make sure you’re saying what really matters on Sunday.
Instead of focusing on the fun and beautiful bits of a life together, get down to the nitty-gritty that actually defines a relationship. Whether this includes financial matters or your emotional needs, the more real you get, the better you will feel about where this connection is headed.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You deserve the love and life you’re dreaming of, Cancer. That includes the home and family, but you must make sure your partner is on the same page as you.
On Sunday, ask the hard questions and genuinely listen to their answers. It may be tempting to think they’ll change their mind eventually or that this will work itself out, but you need to prioritize truth over feelings right now.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Create your own sense of inner safety, Leo. While a relationship should be your safe place in the world, it’s not your partner's responsibility to make you feel safe. You have to be willing to do some of that work on your own.
Learn to trust yourself and provide what you need. This will help you receive a healthy partner and not make them feel like they're carrying the weight of the relationship.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You deserve to be valued, Virgo. That means your partner sees you for all that you are. They don’t take you for granted or dismiss your unique energy as something they can receive from just anyone.

title: Zodiac Love Horoscope, 20th September, 2026: How the cosmic energy encourages honest conversations, clarity, and bold romantic steps
author: Neeraj Dhankher
body:
There will be a desire to enter into relationships without the burden of unnecessary emotional stress. There will be a sense of confidence and attraction. Your Moon is in Sagittarius and Purva Ashadha Nakshatra. You are full of conviction and passion. Single people may feel more confident in their search for a romantic partner. There may be more candour between couples about plans for the future, their feelings or shared experiences.
How to Navigate Today’s Energy
Enjoy the lighter side of love, but don't discount others' feelings. Purva Ashadha can make one strongly believe in their own view and can lead to stubborn disagreements if neither side listens. Couples are encouraged to spend time doing leisure activities, travelling or new experiences. Singles can be attracted to energetic people, but it is important to see whether the attraction remains when the initial excitement fades. The most powerful confidence is that which is accompanied by respect and patience.
Zodiac Signs That Need Care Today
Gemini: You may find yourself with too many romantic options, or you may get mixed signals. Be sure you know what you really want before you commit to it. 
Choosing the simpler options might help you out of your emotional confusion.
Virgo: You may focus too much on the practical shortcomings of someone who otherwise suits your personality. Let the connection develop before you decide whether small differences matter.
Pisces: Your current partner might be acting more independent than you'd like. Don’t interpret their desire for independence as an emotional retreat. Where expectations are less constraining, trust could be enhanced.
Cancer: You may be seeking comfort, while a close relative is looking for adventure or change. Don't take this difference personally.
Zodiac Signs That May Enjoy Good Luck
Scorpio: Your vulnerability is natural and can create a romantic magnetism of great intensity. Singles can connect through shared interests, social events, learning or travel. Disrupt their routines and get couples to rekindle their sense of excitement.
Aries: Your self-confidence could be just what it takes to move a romance forward. A direct invitation, an impromptu plan or an obvious sign of attraction can prompt an encouraging response.
Leo: Your warmth and charm work in your favor. Someone may be more receptive to your advances. The existing relationships can be more playful and loving.
Libra: A romantic opportunity may arise from a social interaction. Your easygoing attitude can help keep the conversation flowing, especially when you’re talking to someone who loves culture, travel, or creative things.
Balanced Day for These Zodiac Signs
Taurus: Slow changes in steady romance.
Scorpio:
 There can be strong feelings, but emotional control can help, and there’s no need for unnecessary tension.
Capricorn: Personal obligations may limit leisure time, but affection is consistent.
Aquarius: A friendship could turn romantic, but there’s no need to put a label on it just yet.
Lucky Action of the Day
Shared enthusiasm can be a spark for attraction and a help for conversation.

Aries Love Horoscope Today:
Single: You could be drawn to someone who sees life differently from you. A different background, belief system or lifestyle may actually be what makes the connection interesting. Let the conversation breathe before deciding where it is going. Sometimes the best chemistry starts with curiosity.
In a relationship: You may want closeness without giving up your independence. Your partner could mistake a little distance for disinterest, especially if you keep your feelings to yourself. A spontaneous outing or simple change of routine can bring back the playful side of your bond.
Married: Venus strengthens your partnership zone, making mutual effort especially important. Do not let family routines or practical responsibilities take over every conversation. A little romance can remind both of you why the relationship works beyond everyday duties.
Love tip: Give space, but stay emotionally present.
Aries Horoscope 2026|Aries Weekly Horoscope| Aries September Horoscope
Taurus Love Horoscope Today:
Single: Your definition of attraction may be quietly changing. Someone who feels steady, thoughtful and emotionally safe could appeal more than a person who keeps you guessing. That is a useful shift. Notice how you feel after speaking to someone, not just the excitement in the moment.
In a relationship: Small issues around effort, attention or expectations may become harder to ignore. Do not turn one awkward moment into a full relationship audit. A calm conversation can clear more than assumptions ever will.
Married: You may need to discuss something practical that carries a deeper emotional layer. Keep the tone gentle. Your partner may be looking less for a solution and more for reassurance that you are both on the same page.
Love tip: Choose emotional safety over mixed signals.

Gemini Love Horoscope Today:
Single: Romance can begin with words today. Someone's humour, confidence or way of thinking may stay on your mind after a conversation ends. There is a nice mental spark around you, but let interest grow naturally before putting a label on it.
In a relationship: Your partnership zone is active, but Mars in your second house can make words sharper than intended. A conversation about money, family or responsibilities could turn personal fast. Watch the tone, especially when you are already annoyed.
Married: Your spouse may respond better to warmth than a perfectly logical explanation. Being right is not always the same as being understood.
Love tip: Protect the bond while discussing the problem.

Cancer Love Horoscope Today:
Single: Love can feel unusually personal today. Mars has moved into Cancer while exalted Jupiter remains here, making you more emotionally invested in who gets close to you. Someone may make you feel genuinely seen, which can be exciting and slightly overwhelming. Enjoy the spark, but let trust build at its own pace.
In a relationship: You may want reassurance but hesitate to ask for it. Do not test your partner by going quiet and waiting for them to notice. Say what is actually bothering you. Honest vulnerability will work better than emotional guessing games.
Married: Your protective side is strong. That can make your spouse feel deeply cared for, but too much involvement in their choices can start feeling restrictive. Support them without taking over.
Love tip: Care deeply without becoming controlling.

Leo Love Horoscope Today:
Single: Romance gets a noticeable lift today. The Sagittarius Moon activates your fifth house of love and attraction, making you more open to flirting, laughter and genuine romantic excitement. Someone could bring out a lighter side of you that has been missing lately. Enjoy it, but look beyond the chemistry.
In a relationship: You may want more affection but feel tempted to act distant instead. That classic “let me see if they chase me” move may not land well. Ask for what you want. It is much easier than decoding each other's behaviour.
Married: A little fun can do more than another serious conversation. Plan a meal out, take a drive or simply do something neither of you normally does together.
Love tip: Ask for affection instead of testing it.

Virgo Love Horoscope Today:
Single: You are likely to notice the little things today. Someone's consistency, tone and behaviour may tell you more than their big statements. Your instincts can be useful, but do not turn every text into a case study. Interest needs observation, not investigation.
In a relationship: Strong Mercury makes it easier to explain what you mean, but it can also make you overanalyse the relationship. Tell your partner what hurt you without presenting a list of evidence. Clarity works better when it still leaves room for empathy.
Married: Family, finances or shared responsibilities may dominate the day. Make space for a conversation that is simply about the two of you, with no problem to solve.
Love tip: Communicate clearly without overanalysing everything.

Libra Love Horoscope Today:
Single: Venus in Libra keeps your charm high, but your standards are changing with it. Attention alone may not impress you anymore. You could feel more drawn to someone who is consistent, emotionally mature and clear about wanting to know you. Peace may finally look more attractive than unpredictability.
In a relationship: You may realise that keeping the peace is not the same as solving the problem. A genuine conversation can bring back emotional warmth, especially if you stop trying to make everything sound fine.
Married: Your presence itself can set the tone at home. A little affection, appreciation or a thoughtful message may shift the mood more than you expect.
Love tip: Choose honest harmony over forced peace.

Scorpio Love Horoscope Today:
Single: You may see a connection more clearly today than you did a few days ago. The Sagittarius Moon shifts attention towards values, priorities and what you actually want to build. Someone attractive may still catch your eye, but confusing behaviour is less likely to feel worth the effort.
In a relationship: A recurring issue may finally reveal its real cause. Try not to bring up every old example just to prove your point. Focus on what is happening now. That is where the relationship can actually move forward.
Married: A discussion around money, family priorities or future plans may need maturity. Keep the conversation focused rather than turning old mistakes into ammunition.
Love tip: Address the issue without reopening every wound.

title: St Columba's pupil travels from Paris to Tahiti after falling in love with languages
author: Susan Lochrie
body:
A FORMER St Columba's High pupil who is now travelling the world after learning to love languages at school returned to the classroom to inspire a new generation.
Anna Gibson, 24, told a group of students how opportunities have opened up for her after falling in love with both French and Spanish in secondary.
She went on to study the languages at university and, after living in Spain and Paris for two years, she is now heading for the Pacific island of Tahiti to teach English.
Anna was invited to back to the Gourock school by Modern languages principal Emma Donnelly to share her experiences and demonstrate how modern languages can impact career opportunities.
The Wemyss Bay woman said: "I have no background in languages at home or anything. When I started secondary I thought I would go down the science and engineering route.
"But I loved learning languages, I learned Spanish first then French. It was my passion and I was so encouraged by Emma and the teachers here. They are so supportive.
"I decided to go for it and do languages at Glasgow University, my parents were supportive and just said do what you love.
"I have never looked back since. I loved uni, I took every opportunity that came my way.
"I ended up teaching in France, I worked in Spain and then I went to live in Paris was two years. I have never said no to any opportunity.
"I am now going to teach English in Tahiti. I never thought imagined this would be my life. It is a dream come true.
"I think it is so important that young people like me know the doors that can open for you if you learn and speak another language."
Anna said: "When you speak the language of a country you understand the culture and the mindset, it unlocks so much more."
Her experiences had a massive impact on the third year pupils who have chosen to study a language at national level.
In Inverclyde schools, modern languages are optional from third year onwards.
Many of the pupils listening to the talk said afterwards that, like Anna, they want to travel.
Among them Anna Nelis told the Tele: "I love Spanish and I really want to travel. I was really impressed listening to Anna."
Modern languages principal Ms Donnelly said: "It was wonderful to have Anna here. She is incredible and has taken every opportunity. Anna is the perfect example of what you can achieve with languages.
"I heard some of the pupils saying that they were re-evaluating their lives following her talk."

title: Dear Abby: My co-workers smirk and stare because of my failed romance
author: Abigail Van Buren
body:
DEAR ABBY: I am a man in my 40s. A woman and I had a relationship that ended badly. We met on the job.
Everyone at work knows about our former relationship, and it is extremely awkward, though we are in different departments. Every time I walk by, there are lots of smiles and chattering; when I approach my co-workers’ desks, I’m greeted with silence and intense stares.
I still have strong feelings for her, and I know they are reciprocated because she has verbalized it and shown it with her actions and behaviors.
After she ended things, I was upset and gave her the silent treatment. I know she feels hurt by my pretending like she doesn’t exist. I am a stubborn man, but I really miss her.
After the breakup, she mentioned being friends. I cannot be friends with her.
Despite the amount of time that has gone by, I still want to fix things. However, I know my real intentions and illusions about getting back together are misguided fantasy. I would appreciate your insights.
— AWKWARD AT WORK
DEAR AWKWARD: Do you understand that it’s you, not your co-workers, making things awkward? By resorting to the silent treatment, you’ve made everyone uncomfortable.
You say you want to fix things, but you’ve made no attempt to do so. You don’t believe you can reconcile with your ex, but on what grounds? You won’t even talk to her!
I don’t think you’re “stubborn”; I think you’re afraid. You’ve kept up this unseemly behavior because you don’t want to be hurt again.
If you can’t muster the courage to tell this woman you want another chance, you have two options left: Either speak with her purely as a colleague and bury the hatchet so you can at least be cordial in the workplace, or start looking for another job.
DEAR ABBY: My father’s girlfriend, “Jane,” has started soliciting money for her causes from everyone she knows, especially our family members.
After the first request, I donated a modest amount to support her, not knowing the deluge of requests that would follow. I have a set amount of money I can use for charity and would rather decide for myself how to spend it.
Jane and my father are sensitive about her being accepted into our family. They both tend to look for slights and then blow them out of proportion. Dad has made it clear that unless my siblings and I fully embrace Jane, he won’t be part of our lives.
I admire him sticking up for her, but I know if I decline the next donation request it’s going to get ugly. I feel like I’m being held hostage. How do I get out of this situation?
— HELD HOSTAGE IN VANCOUVER
DEAR HELD HOSTAGE: Talk to your father privately and tell him you love him. Remind him that you don’t have an unlimited amount of money to donate to charity, that you have causes of your own that are important to you, and that you have already donated to Jane’s more than once. Ask him to explain that to her and that it isn’t a rejection of her — just fiscal responsibility on your part.
He needs to know you feel like you won’t be able to have a relationship with the father you adore if you refuse these solicitations.
Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips wrote this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.

DEAR ABBY: I am a man in my 40s. A woman and I had a relationship that ended badly. We met on the job.
Everyone at work knows about our former relationship, and it is extremely awkward, though we are in different departments. Every time I walk by, there are lots of smiles and chattering; when I approach my co-workers’ desks, I’m greeted with silence and intense stares.
I still have strong feelings for her, and I know they are reciprocated because she has verbalized it and shown it with her actions and behaviors.
After she ended things, I was upset and gave her the silent treatment. I know she feels hurt by my pretending like she doesn’t exist. I am a stubborn man, but I really miss her.
After the breakup, she mentioned being friends. I cannot be friends with her.
Despite the amount of time that has gone by, I still want to fix things. However, I know my real intentions and illusions about getting back together are misguided fantasy. I would appreciate your insights.
— AWKWARD AT WORK
DEAR AWKWARD: Do you understand that it’s you, not your co-workers, making things awkward? By resorting to the silent treatment, you’ve made everyone uncomfortable.
You say you want to fix things, but you’ve made no attempt to do so. You don’t believe you can reconcile with your ex, but on what grounds? You won’t even talk to her!
I don’t think you’re “stubborn”; I think you’re afraid. You’ve kept up this unseemly behavior because you don’t want to be hurt again.
If you can’t muster the courage to tell this woman you want another chance, you have two options left: Either speak with her purely as a colleague and bury the hatchet so you can at least be cordial in the workplace, or start looking for another job.
DEAR ABBY: My father’s girlfriend, “Jane,” has started soliciting money for her causes from everyone she knows, especially our family members.
After the first request, I donated a modest amount to support her, not knowing the deluge of requests that would follow. I have a set amount of money I can use for charity and would rather decide for myself how to spend it.
Jane and my father are sensitive about her being accepted into our family. They both tend to look for slights and then blow them out of proportion. Dad has made it clear that unless my siblings and I fully embrace Jane, he won’t be part of our lives.
I admire him sticking up for her, but I know if I decline the next donation request it’s going to get ugly. I feel like I’m being held hostage. How do I get out of this situation?
— HELD HOSTAGE IN VANCOUVER
DEAR HELD HOSTAGE: Talk to your father privately and tell him you love him. Remind him that you don’t have an unlimited amount of money to donate to charity, that you have causes of your own that are important to you, and that you have already donated to Jane’s more than once. Ask him to explain that to her and that it isn’t a rejection of her — just fiscal responsibility on your part.
He needs to know you feel like you won’t be able to have a relationship with the father you adore if you refuse these solicitations.
Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips wrote this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.

title: Blind date: ‘We talked about how I don’t like Clapham gays – guess where he lives?’
author: Guardian Staff; Guardian staff reporter
body:
Dec on Dave
What were you hoping for?
 A sweet-hearted madman who would make me belly laugh.
First impressions?
 Looked like a David. A bit nervous and jittery, but considerate, curious and chatty (all the best C-words).
What did you talk about?
 People in cars shouting “ginge” at him. Us coming from the West Country (but only I sound like it). How I don’t like Clapham gays – guess where he lives?
Most awkward moment?
 I tried on his stethoscope, pretending to listen for a heartbeat from the chicken.
Good table manners?
 Sound as a pound.
Best thing about David?
 His passion for his profession. Also, how he was so keen to ask, listen and hear.
Would you introduce David to your friends?
 Possibly, so they can give him his second Buzzballz ever!
Describe David in three words
 Moustached, kind, grounded.
What do you think David made of you?
 Probably an absolute loony. No, I wonder if he saw through the tarty humour to my kind, smart, caring self.
Did you go on somewhere?
 The kitchen was closing, and he had to work in the morning, saving lives – very inconsiderate.
And … did you kiss?
 I gave him a polite peck on the cheek when we hugged bye-bye.
If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
 Nothing: it was the perfect balance of sincere connection and nonsense.
Marks out of 10?
 A solid 6. He’s a cracking bloke and rocks a floral shirt better than anyone I know. It’s a 6 not a 7 because I don’t like fish or salad; he kindly ordered me both.
Would you meet again?
 We swapped numbers. We’re not each other’s “spark”, but had a good evening.
David on Dec
What were you hoping for?
 Someone who put me at ease, asked me questions and made me want to text my friends about him in the toilet.
First impressions?
 Definitely a main character. Handsome, potty-mouthed, charming and equally clueless about tapas.
What did you talk about?
 Dec’s love of swearing. Coming out.
Most awkward moment?
 Possibly when I realised I had a child’s blood on my trousers.
Good table manners?
 Impeccable.
Best thing about Dec?
 He’s very free and at ease in himself, and made me feel I could be too. And his autobiography will be a bestseller.
Would you introduce Dec to your friends?
 I would. But I didn’t toilet-text them.
Describe Dec in three words
 Curious, beautiful, free.
What do you think Dec made of you?
 Hopefully good company! “Doctor” brings a whole set of expectations, but it felt like he was able to see past all that.
Did you go on somewhere?
 We didn’t – but we stayed until closing.
And … did you kiss?
 A quick peck at the station.
If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be?
 We were side-by-side at the bar, which is weird for a first date. And he got my right side, which is definitely less good.
Marks out of 10?
 8.
Would you meet again?
 We agreed the chemistry felt more friendly than romantic, but I’d love to stay in touch.
Dec and David ate at Barrafina Drury Lane, London WC2. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com

title: Oakridge expert shares relationship advice inspired by Dua Lipa
author: Stroud News; Journal Staff
body:
Column by Penny Newton-Hurley
DUA Lipa recently shared her wedding advice: experience the day as a guest would and stay close to your husband.
Both concern being present and connected each day.
That matters beyond the wedding.
Long-term relationships can falter when practical conversations replace emotional ones.
We talk about school runs, shopping, bills and appointments, but stop asking: “How are you, really?”
When a partner says, “You’re never here,” the words may sound accusing.
Underneath them might be loneliness and a longing for closeness.
The listener hears criticism and replies defensively: “I’m working to support us.”
Now both people are protecting themselves and neither feels understood.
Try slowing the exchange down.
Separate the fact from the judgement, identify the feeling and consider what is needed.
“I’ve noticed we haven’t spent an evening together this week. I miss you and would love time to reconnect. Could we keep Friday evening free?”
This does not guarantee the answer will be yes.
But it makes connection more likely than blame does.
This approach is part of the four-stage MECAnism in my book, The Human Language, out now.
It helps us recognise our thoughts, emotions and core needs before deciding what to say or do.
Staying close on a wedding day is lovely advice.
Staying curious, emotionally honest and connected throughout the days that follow is what sustains a relationship.
The photographs may capture the celebration, but it is the quieter conversations afterwards that build a marriage.
Penny Newton-Hurley is an Oakridge-based communication consultant and mediator.
Her new book, The Human Language, is out now, priced £12.99, and available from bookshops and Amazon.

title: Forget dating apps – Try charming the Home Office over the phone
author: Alistair McNair
body:
I’ve just tried blind speed-dating. Missed it in my twenties. Was too square.
Now in a spasm of late forties’ angst I’ve spent hours calling total strangers trying to make them like me.
I didn’t ever think I’d end up speed-dating. Didn’t think the wife would approve – or that would-be girl for that matter. I’m a bit out of practice – and out of shape let’s face it. But after this week, like a 49-year-old virgin on a first date, I’ve become something of a silver-tongued suitor. Just not on the right people. I’m told girls love questions. It shows you care. But I’ve discovered that civil servants on the end of a phone don’t. Even if they’re called Shahida.
My wife Tetiana needed a share code. It’s an electronic ID. A random mix of numbers and letters the government gives you if you’re not a citizen so you can work, rent or, in our case, get a mortgage. They should just tattoo it on your arm when you first arrive at Dover. There’s an idea Nigel.
Now, Tetiana has been in the country since 2009. She has Indefinite Leave to Remain. Stamped in her passport – two passports ago. She’s allowed in even though in her fur coat she looks like a Romanian people smuggler. She can be let loose on a mental health clinic but she can’t vote. Then three months into the remortgaging process, our mortgage advisor suddenly tells us they don’t accept paper visas. Although they did five years ago. You need a share code.
How do you get a share code? First, you set up a UKVI – UK Visas and Immigration – online account. Then they make you shlep all the way to Croydon to give your biometrics. It’s deliberate. If the office was in Hove, no one would ever leave the country. But who would want to stay in the UK after going to Croydon? In reality, most people who go to Croydon for a visa never actually leave. Because, trouble is, once Rick Deckard has bagged up your blood, hair, toenail clippings and fingerprints, you’re in no fit state to go anywhere else. So that’s Croydon.
And then you wait. And wait. Now a mortgage has a deadline. If you think you’re clobbered by your interest rate now, wait till you go on the standard variable rate. We had until September 23. Where was our share code? Silly me. Who’s going to catch any Home Office civil servant worth their salt working in August? Or even in England. I started to look up by-elections in Scotland to help make ends meet.
So, deep breath, we decide to phone UKVI. This is where speed dating skills come in handy. If Ovid was alive today, he wouldn’t write about the Minotaur – that horned cow at the centre of a labyrinth. No. He’d write about UKVI phone options. Because before you get to impress anyone with your wit, you need to press number 4. Then number 2. Then number 4. Then number 4 again. Then number 2. There are more numbers called out than during a night at Mecca bingo. Advisors are more protected from foreign reach than our gold bullion under Threadneedle Street.
It wouldn’t be so bad if it wasn’t a different advisor each time. “Calls may be recorded for training and data protection purposes.” Not to actually relieve you from having to tell them your problem all over again each time. And that’s before you’ve got past security. How long is your inside leg? What’s your cat’s middle name? Someone suddenly speaks: “How can I help you?” Can I remember how to speak English? “My wife needs a share code.” I hope he can smell my aftershave. Can pheromones travel down the phone line? “Have you got a UKVI account?” “Yes.” “Hang on a minute.”
Something in his voice told me this potential lover would never find my wife’s electronic data. My wife and I decide to tag team. The music stops and it’s time to move on. By the end of the night, no one’s marked my score card. Not even the wife.
All I can say is Tetiana must have more experience kissing frogs than me. However she wooed him, it worked. She probably chanced upon someone on day release from some luxury hotel that provides all day breakfast. With the speed and grace of a concierge at the Ritz, it took this marvel of productivity fewer than five minutes to fix my wife’s share code.
You can order swarms of bees on Amazon but if the state loses your data, it’s like looking for a yellow Lego brick in a children’s sand pit. Pity help us when the replicants take over.
Alistair McNair is Leader of the Conservatives on Brighton and Hove City Council.
